uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The UK's monthly consumer price index, compiled by the Office for National Statistics. It is the measure the Bank of England's inflation target is written against, and it feeds index-linked gilts, pensions and a range of regulated prices.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: This release settles what UK consumer prices did in September, in a single figure published in one go. Nothing on the record yet marks it out from a routine month.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the US overnight policy rate. It prices the world's reserve currency, so its decisions reach borrowing costs well beyond the United States.
fomc-2026-10.recent: September's vote was 12-0 to raise, taken against Trump's public calls to cut and against an inflation the committee cannot reach: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in August with Brent near $110 after the Houthis took Yemen's port of Mocha. What October settles is whether a closed strait is a shock to look through or one to keep tightening into.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets the single policy rate for the twenty countries sharing the euro. It meets every six weeks, and its decisions reach borrowing costs from Dublin to Athens through one instrument for economies that rarely move together.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term rate and guide government bond yields. Because Japan is the world's largest creditor nation, the cost of borrowing yen is a funding input for markets far beyond it.
boj-2026-10.recent: The board arrives at this meeting having just taken the rate to 1.25%, a 31-year high, to curb rising prices — and the yen fell rather than rose afterwards, which is a market saying the move did not go far enough. Ueda's 75-minute briefing did not settle the question, and Tokyo is separately weighing whether pension money should be steered to defend the currency.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate — the floor under mortgage and business borrowing costs. Each member's vote is published, so the split is read as closely as the decision itself.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee meets with Brent settled near $106 a barrel, an imported price shock no policy rate can reach, and with the Fed having raised in a unanimous vote and the Bank of Japan having taken its own rate to 1.25%. What this decision settles is the cost of borrowing for the households and firms already carrying the energy bill.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the twelve-member body that sets the US federal funds rate at eight scheduled meetings a year. It prices dollar credit worldwide, and because so much of global trade and borrowing is denominated in dollars, its decisions reach far beyond American borrowers.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The committee arrives at this meeting having already raised rates in a unanimous 12-0 vote in September, tightening into a supply shock rather than a demand boom — the cause was a closed strait, and August consumer prices rose 0.4% as the war reached the price index. Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call before that decision. What December settles is whether the Fed keeps tightening against an oil price it cannot influence.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of the leaders of the world's twenty largest economies, hosted by a presidency that rotates each year and sets the agenda. It has no treaty power; its output is a communiqué, and its weight comes from who agrees to sign one.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets the single policy rate for the twenty countries that use the euro. Its decisions reach borrowing costs for some 350 million people across economies with very different exposures.
ecb-2026-12.recent: The council meets with the euro area's inflation problem running through an energy bill it cannot influence, and Deutsche Bank has already raised its expected ECB peak to 2.75% on that basis. What this decision settles is how far the council is willing to tighten against a price shock imported through fuel, and whether it treats second-round transmission into wages and services as the thing it must act on.

boe-2026-12.standing: The United Kingdom's central bank, whose Monetary Policy Committee votes eight times a year on Bank Rate — the rate that sets the price of credit for households and firms across Britain, and that sterling and gilt yields move with.
boe-2026-12.recent: Rate-setters meet after an oil shock that carried Brent near $106 a barrel and drove peers to tighten: the Federal Reserve raised in a unanimous vote, and the Bank of Japan went to a 31-year high. What this decision settles is whether an imported price rise the committee cannot reach is leaned against, and the cost of borrowing follows that judgement.

boj-2026-12.standing: Japan's central bank sets its policy rate at eight scheduled meetings a year. Because yen borrowing has been the cheapest in the developed world for decades, what it decides prices funding for investors far outside Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: The September hike landed badly: the yen fell rather than rose, and the governor's 75-minute briefing failed to win over markets. December is the next chance to settle whether that move was read as too small — with a currency Tokyo has weighed defending through pension money, and a balancing act with Bessent that is only going to get harder.
